arxiv-1510-01438.title: Anomalous magnetic response of a quasi-periodic mesoscopic ring in presence of Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit interactions
arxiv-1510-01438.creator: Moumita Patra, Santanu K. Maiti
arxiv-1510-01438.description: Abstract We investigate the properties of persistent charge current driven by magnetic flux in a quasi-periodic mesoscopic Fibonacci ring with Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit interactions. Within a tight-binding framework we work out individual state currents together with net current based on second-quantized approach.

arxiv-2104-08835.title: in Proc. of EMNLP 2021 CrossFit : A Few-shot Learning Challenge for Cross-task Generalization in NLP
arxiv-2104-08835.creator: Qinyuan Ye, Bill Yuchen Lin, Xiang Ren
arxiv-2104-08835.description: Abstract Humans can learn a new language task efficiently with only few examples, by leveraging their knowledge obtained when learning prior tasks. In this paper, we explore whether and how such cross-task generalization ability can be acquired, and further applied to build better few-shot learners across diverse NLP tasks.

arxiv-2108-11114.title: Quantum kernels with squeezed-state encoding for machine learning
arxiv-2108-11114.creator: Long Hin Li, Dan-Bo Zhang, Z. D. Wang
arxiv-2108-11114.description: Abstract Kernel methods are powerful for machine learning, as they can represent data in feature spaces that similarities between samples may be faithfully captured. Recently, it is realized that machine learning enhanced by quantum computing is closely related to kernel methods, where the exponentially large Hilbert space turns to be a feature space more expressive than classical ones.

arxiv-2111-13859.title: Asymptotic spectra of large (grid) graphs with a uniform local structure (part II): numerical applications
arxiv-2111-13859.creator: Andrea Adriani, Davide Bianchi, Paola Ferrari, Stefano Serra-Capizzano
arxiv-2111-13859.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Andrea Adriani, Davide Bianchi, Paola Ferrari, Stefano Serra-Capizzano. In the current work we are concerned with sequences of graphs having a grid geometry, with a uniform local structure in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ d \Omega\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{d} , d ≥ 1 d\geq 1 . When Ω = [ 0 , 1 ] \Omega=[0,1] , such graphs include the standard Toeplitz graphs and, for Ω = [ 0 , 1 ] d \Omega=[0,1]^{d} , the considered class includes d d -level Toeplitz graphs.

arxiv-2207-07548.title: Global existence and singularity formation for the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda equation with dissipation: The real line vs. periodic domains
arxiv-2207-07548.creator: David M. Ambrose, Pavel M. Lushnikov, Michael Siegel, Denis A. Silantyev
arxiv-2207-07548.description: Abstract The question of global existence versus finite-time singularity formation is considered for the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda equation with dissipation − Λ σ -\Lambda^{\sigma} , where Λ σ ^ = | k | σ \widehat{{\Lambda}^{\sigma}}=|k|^{\sigma} , both for the problem on the circle x ∈ [ − π , π ] x\in[-\pi,\pi] and the real line.

arxiv-2207-10557.title: Automorphisms of 𝒫 ⁡ ( ω ) / fin \mathcal{P}(\omega)/\mbox{fin} and large continuum
arxiv-2207-10557.creator: Alan Dow
arxiv-2207-10557.description: Abstract . We prove that it is consistent with 𝔠 > ℵ 2 \mathfrak{c}>\aleph_{2} that all automorphisms of 𝒫 ⁡ ( ω ) / fin \mathcal{P}(\omega)/\mbox{fin} are trivial. 1. Introduction The study of automorphisms of \mathcal{P}(\omega)/\mbox{fin} has, by now, an extensive and fascinating history.

arxiv-2307-12521.title: Steinberg’s cross-section of Newton strata
arxiv-2307-12521.creator: Sian Nie
arxiv-2307-12521.description: Abstract . In this note, we introduce a natural analogue of Steinberg’s cross-section in the loop group of a reductive group 𝐆 \mathbf{G} . We show this loop Steinberg’s cross-section provides a simple geometric model for the poset B ⁡ ( 𝐆 ) B(\mathbf{G}) of Frobenius-twisted conjugacy classes (referred to as Newton strata) of the loop group.

arxiv-2309-05934.title: MatSciML: A Broad, Multi-Task Benchmark for Solid-State Materials Modeling
arxiv-2309-05934.creator: Kin Long Kelvin Lee, Carmelo Gonzales, Marcel Nassar, Matthew Spellings, Mikhail Galkin, Santiago Miret
arxiv-2309-05934.description: Abstract We propose MatSci ML, a novel benchmark for modeling Mat erials Sci ence using M achine L earning methods focused on solid-state materials with periodic crystal structures. Applying machine learning methods to solid-state materials is a nascent field with substantial fragmentation largely driven by the great variety of datasets used to develop machine learning models.

arxiv-2312-00502.title: Which Augmentation Should I Use? An Empirical Investigation of Augmentations for Self-Supervised Phonocardiogram Representation Learning
arxiv-2312-00502.creator: ARISTOTELIS BALLAS 1, VASILEIOS PAPAPANAGIOTOU 2, CHRISTOS DIOU 1
arxiv-2312-00502.description: Abstract Despite recent advancements in deep learning, its application in real-world medical settings, such as phonocardiogram (PCG) classification, remains limited. A significant barrier is the lack of high-quality annotated datasets, which hampers the development of robust, generalizable models that can perform well on newly collected, out-of-distribution (OOD) data.

arxiv-2401-06958.title: Carrollian Born-Infeld Electrodynamics
arxiv-2401-06958.creator: Aditya Mehra, Hemant Rathi, Dibakar Roychowdhury
arxiv-2401-06958.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Aditya Mehra, Hemant Rathi, Dibakar Roychowdhury. In this paper, we carry out a detailed investigation on Born-Infeld (BI) Electrodynamics in its Carrollian limit. We show that the BI Electrodynamics in its Carrollian limit, differs significantly from its conformal Carrollian cousin. For example, the full conformal Carroll symmetry group is broken due to the presence of nonlinear interactions among U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) gauge fields.

arxiv-2411-17784.title: HypDAE : Hyperbolic Diffusion Autoencoders for Hierarchical Few-shot Image Generation
arxiv-2411-17784.creator: Lingxiao Li, Kaixuan Fan, Boqing Gong, Xiangyu Yue
arxiv-2411-17784.description: Abstract Few-shot image generation aims to generate diverse and high-quality images for an unseen class given only a few examples in that class. A key challenge in this task is balancing category consistency and image diversity, which often compete with each other. Moreover, existing methods offer limited control over the attributes of newly generated images.

arxiv-2412-04242.title: LMDM:Latent Molecular Diffusion Model For 3D Molecule Generation
arxiv-2412-04242.creator: Xiang Chen
arxiv-2412-04242.description: Abstract In this work, we propose a latent molecular diffusion model that can make the generated 3D molecules rich in diversity and maintain rich geometric features. The model captures the information of the forces and local constraints between atoms so that the generated molecules can maintain Euclidean transformation and high level of effectiveness and diversity.

arxiv-2502-07029.title: Leveraging Allophony in Self-Supervised Speech Models for Atypical Pronunciation Assessment
arxiv-2502-07029.creator: Kwanghee Choi, Eunjung Yeo, Kalvin Chang, Shinji Watanabe, David Mortensen
arxiv-2502-07029.description: Abstract Allophony refers to the variation in the phonetic realization of a phoneme based on its phonetic environment. Modeling allophones is crucial for atypical pronunciation assessment, which involves distinguishing atypical from typical pronunciations. However, recent phoneme classifier-based approaches often simplify this by treating various realizations as a single phoneme, bypassing the complexity of modeling allophonic variation.

arxiv-2506-05984.title: Audio-Aware Large Language Models as Judges for Speaking Styles
arxiv-2506-05984.creator: Cheng-Han Chiang, Xiaofei Wang, Chung-Ching Lin, Kevin Lin, Linjie Li, Radu Kopetz, Yao Qian, Zhendong Wang, Zhengyuan Yang, Hung-yi Lee, Lijuan Wang
arxiv-2506-05984.description: Abstract Audio-aware large language models (ALLMs) can understand the textual and non-textual information in the audio input. In this paper, we explore using ALLMs as an automatic judge to assess the speaking styles of speeches. We use ALLM judges to evaluate the speeches generated by SLMs on two tasks: voice style instruction following and role-playing.

arxiv-2508-06675.title: A scalable photonic quantum interconnect platform
arxiv-2508-06675.creator: Daniel Riedel, Teodoro Graziosi, Zhuoxian Wang, Chawina De-Eknamkul, Alex Abulnaga, Jonathan Dietz, Andrea Mucchietto, Michael Haas, Madison Sutula, Pierre Barral, Matteo Pompili, Carsten Robens, Jeonghoon Ha, Denis Sukachev, David Levonian, Mihir Bhaskar, Matthew Markham, Bartholomeus Machielse
arxiv-2508-06675.description: Abstract Many quantum networking applications require efficient photonic interfaces to quantum memories which can be produced at scale and with high yield. Synthetic diamond offers unique potential for the implementation of this technology as it hosts color centers which retain coherent optical interfaces and long spin coherence times in nanophotonic structures.

arxiv-2510-11908.title: A gallery of open problems in geometry that keep me puzzled and amused
arxiv-2510-11908.creator: Anton Petrunin
arxiv-2510-11908.description: Abstract This is a collection of open problems in geometry that I think of as puzzles : they stick to my brain — I see many grips, but no spare hands. Puzzle-charm is the only criterion for including a problem here; importance is ignored.

pmc-10628342.title: Is ipsilateral administration of COVID-19 vaccine boosters the optimal approach?
pmc-10628342.creator: Laura Ziegler, Verena Klemis, Tina Schmidt, Sophie Schneitler, Christina Baum, Jürgen Neumann, Sören L Becker, Barbara C Gärtner, Urban Sester, Martina Sester
pmc-10628342.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). at ipsilateral vaccination was associated with a more favourable immune response, and have made a valuable contribution to extend our discussion regarding the underlying mechanisms and relevance of our findings for further COVID-19 immunization events and other vaccines. While ipsilateral vaccination may benefit from the use of the same draining lymph node for priming and boosting, the colleagues speculated that contralateral vaccination may de novo mobilize B-cell clones not previously utilized.

pmc-11393346.title: Histidine-rich glycoprotein modulates neutrophils and thrombolysis-associated hemorrhagic transformation
pmc-11393346.creator: Wei Jiang, Yuexin Zhao, Rongrong Liu, Bohao Zhang, Yuhan Xie, Bin Gao, Kaibin Shi, Ming Zou, Dongmei Jia, Jiayue Ding, Xiaowei Hu, Yanli Duan, Ranran Han, DeRen Huang, Luc Van Kaer, Fu-Dong Shi
pmc-11393346.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Intravenous thrombolysis using recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) remains the primary treatment for patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). However, the mechanism of tPA-related hemorrhagic transformation (HT) remains poorly understood. Elevation of histidine-rich glycoprotein (HRG) expression was detected by nano-liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry at 1 h following tPA infusion as compared to baseline prior to tPA infusion (discovery cohort, n = 10), which was subsequently confirmed in a validation cohort (n = 157) by ELISA.

pmc-12822159.title: Continuous secretory production in E. coli enables scalable, high-titer manufacturing of active recombinant endonucleases
pmc-12822159.creator: Sudarsana Reddy Lokireddy, Chennakesavulu Thummadhi, Pratyusha Godavarty, Venkateswarlu Petla, Akhila Munimanda, Sridhar Rao Kunchala, Ramakrishna Vadde
pmc-12822159.description: Recombinant endonucleases are essential for biopharmaceutical manufacturing and molecular biology workflows, yet their intracellular expression in Escherichia coli often leads to host cell toxicity due to non-specific DNA and RNA degradation. To address this, we employed the BacSec® system to secrete Serratia marcescens non-specific endonuclease, nucA (DRNase®) and bovine DNase I in E.

pmc-13079569.title: Preoperative differentiation of acute appendicitis using NLR, SII, and maximum appendiceal diameter: a retrospective single-center diagnostic study
pmc-13079569.creator: Xu Junyan, Zhang Tao
pmc-13079569.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundRapid classification on Accurate preoperative differentiation between uncomplicated (UCAA) and complicated acute appendicitis (CAA) is essential for guiding treatment but remains challenging. Existing tools, such as clinical scores and common inflammatory markers, lack sufficient accuracy for reliable stratification.MethodsIn this retrospective single-center study, 207 patients with pathologically confirmed appendicitis (52 UCAA, 155 CAA) undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy between June 2024 and September 2025 were analyzed.

pmc-13092009.title: Impact of gut microbiome, plasma metabolites, peripheral immune cells, and circulating inflammatory protein on chronic spontaneous urticaria: Bidirectional 2-sample Mendelian randomization study and mediation analysis
pmc-13092009.creator: Lijun Deng, Yuxu Yao, Qian Wang, Zhenzhong Lu, Enze Li, Ying Hu, Jialu Chen, Guoli Wang, Tingting Yu, Jiang Ji, Qingqing Jiao
pmc-13092009.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundGrowing evidence links gut microbiota to chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), yet causality and underlying mediators remain unclear.ObjectiveWe investigated causal relationships and potential mediators—specifically plasma metabolites, immune cells, and inflammatory proteins—through which gut microbes influence CSU risk.MethodsWe applied 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to genome-wide association study (GWAS) data on 430 gut microbial taxa, 1,400 plasma metabolites, 731 immune cell traits, and 91 inflammatory proteins.

pmc-13168245.title: Conformational landscape of HIV-1 Env from closed to fully open
pmc-13168245.creator: Jiayan Cui, Zi Jie Lin, Sukanya Ghosh, Jianqiu Du, Roopak Sadeesh, David B. Weiner, Jesper Pallesen
pmc-13168245.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The molecular mechanism of HIV-1 entry into host cells is governed by dynamic conformational changes to its envelope glycoprotein (Env), which are triggered by the engagement of the host receptor CD4 and coreceptors. Structural insights into these transitions have been advanced by cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET), resolving Env structures in closed and multifarious open states within native membranes, and by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), which has provided atomic details of these states.

pmc-13402642.title: Exploring Australian Health Promotion Practitioners’ Awareness, Understanding and Application of Theories of the Policy Process in Health Promotion Practice: A Qualitative Study
pmc-13402642.creator: Rhian Jones, Kara Lilly, Rachel Cole
pmc-13402642.description: Introduction: Theories of the policy process provide structured ways to understand, navigate and influence political landscapes using evidence-based approaches. While influencing policy is a core function of the health promotion discipline, little is known about how practitioners engage with these theories.

pmc-13427579.title: A dataset for material-specific packaging volumes in Finland in 2020
pmc-13427579.creator: Henna Jylhä, Annika Johansson, Jani Salminen
pmc-13427579.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The European Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation sets targets for reducing the use of packaging materials and for improving packaging recycling. Monitoring related to these targets requires comparable data on total packaging volumes in each EU member state. Packaging accounting methodology, which relies on annually reported packaging data obtained from producer responsibility organizations, and standard economic statistics compiled by national statistical office, provides a solid approach to quantifying the total volume of packaging placed on the market within a country.

pmc-13454076.title: Activating Cannabinoid receptor 2 alleviates iron overload-induced liver damage via dual modulation of STAT3/hepcidin and Nrf2/FPN1 pathways
pmc-13454076.creator: Han Deng, Yuqian Ren, Yunjie Sui, Zegang Ma
pmc-13454076.description: Iron overload-related liver injury is a major clinical problem in hereditary hemochromatosis, transfusional siderosis, and chronic liver diseases, yet current treatments such as iron chelation therapy and phlebotomy are limited by safety and efficacy issues. Cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2R) has been implicated in the regulation of iron metabolism, but its role and underlying mechanism in iron overload remain unclear.
